title: 2025 Bum Bowl
dek: The 2025 Bum Bowl was the last-place game of the Buckaroo Football League's third season, in which Ramon's Remains beat Dawgs 97.58 to 93.58 in NFL Week 17 and Dawgs finished sixth of six.
body: The 2025 Bum Bowl was the final rung of the Buckaroo Football League's consolation ladder, the bracket that decides last place. It was played over a single NFL week, Week 17, between Ramon's Remains, the fifth seed, and Dawgs, the fourth seed. The loser would finish sixth of six and take the league's least wanted distinction. That honor had belonged to Sonny's Ben Dover in both 2023 and 2024, but Sonny spent 2025 winning Buckaroo Bowl III instead, so the 2025 Bum Bowl was guaranteed to produce a new name at the bottom.

Dawgs, managed by Mekhi, finished the regular season 8-8 with 1,858.2 points, about 116.1 per week. That was 334.5 points more than Ramon's Remains managed, a gap that made Dawgs' presence in the last-place game one of the stranger outcomes of the season. Mekhi, who drafted that year from basic training, had a roster with real firepower, including Christian McCaffrey, Josh Allen and Jahmyr Gibbs, and by points alone the team looked like anything but a Bum Bowl participant.

Ramon's Remains went 5-11 with 1,523.7 points, roughly 95.2 per week. The team began the year as Araleasers under Ramon, who ran it through Week 8 before being removed from the league for inactivity. It was renamed Ramon's Remains and played out the season without him, and under league rules those games still counted on Ramon's record, marked with an asterisk. The 2025 Bum Bowl was therefore a game Brucie won without being in the league.

The two sides met three times in the regular season. Dawgs won the first two comfortably, 125.22 to 91.3 in Week 5 and 137.14 to 88.5 in Week 10, before Ramon's Remains took the third, 105.26 to 99.32, in Week 15. Neither manager entered with a championship; both Buckaroo Bowls before 2025 had gone to Kaushal's Habibsters, and the league's records show no earlier postseason meeting between these two managers.

The league's records for this game do not detail the earlier rounds of the 2025 consolation ladder, so the individual results and performers that sent each team into the Bum Bowl are not documented here. What is recorded is that both teams missed the championship bracket and ended up in the last-place game, with Dawgs seeded fourth and Ramon's Remains fifth.

For Dawgs, the path ran against the grain of the season's scoring. A team that averaged more than 116 points a week and split its 16 games evenly found itself in the final game of the consolation ladder. For Ramon's Remains, the path continued the strange afterlife of a roster with no manager, which had already beaten Dawgs once in December, in the Week 15 meeting, just two weeks before the Bum Bowl.

The game was decided entirely in NFL Week 17. No play-by-play was recorded for it, since the league website only began saving in-game events in Week 7 of 2026, so the order of scoring within the week is not known. Ramon's Remains won 97.58 to 93.58, a margin of exactly 4 points.

Going by projections, Ramon's Remains was a slight favorite. Its starters were projected for a combined 112.0 points against 107.6 for Dawgs. Both lineups fell well short: Ramon's Remains finished 14.4 points under its projection and Dawgs 14.0 under, so the favorite held on by close to the margin it was expected to win by.

Ramon's Remains was carried by running back Chase Brown, who scored 27.6 points in his first start for the team, and by quarterback Dak Prescott, who added 22.7. Those two accounted for 50.3 of the team's 97.58 points. The rest of the lineup was thin: Puka Nacua managed 13.2, Travis Etienne Jr. 10.2, and Jaylen Waddle just 0.7.

Dawgs got 26.1 points from McCaffrey and 23.2 from Allen, with Kyren Williams adding 14.5 and Jordan Addison 12.5. The damage came from the bottom of the lineup, where Gibbs scored 5.4, Drake London 0.9, Cameron Dicker 3, and tight end Dalton Kincaid 0. Dawgs finished 93.58, more than 22 points below its regular-season average, on the one week it could least afford it.

Chase Brown was the game's top scorer at 27.6 points, nearly double his 14.3-point projection, in what was his first start for Ramon's Remains. Prescott beat his 20.5-point projection with 22.7, above his 16.5-point average in three earlier starts for the team. On the Dawgs side, McCaffrey scored 26.1 against a 22.8 projection and a 22.1 season average, and Allen put up 23.2 against an 18.3 projection. The Bills quarterback starring for the team trying to beat Brucie's was a small irony, given Ramon's Bills fandom. Addison, projected for 7.3, delivered 12.5, and the Rams D/ST scored 8 against a 5.3 projection.

The flops decided the game. Gibbs, who had averaged 20.3 points in 15 starts and was projected for 18.5, scored 5.4. London scored 0.9 against a 12.8 projection, and Dicker, a 10.1-point-per-start kicker, managed 3. For Ramon's Remains, Waddle's 0.7 came against a 10.8 projection, Jaylen Warren scored 6.4 against 12.6, and Nacua's 13.2 sat well below his 18.6 average across 13 starts.

The most consequential lineup decision was at tight end. Kincaid was started with a projection of 0 and scored 0, while Oronde Gadsden sat on the Dawgs bench with 10.7 points. That swap alone would have lifted Dawgs to 104.28 and won the game. Khalil Shakir's 6.5 points on the bench would also have outscored London's 0.9, and Rico Dowdle's 7.8 topped Gibbs's 5.4. Baker Mayfield's 17.4 on the bench would not have helped, as Allen outscored him.

Ramon's Remains left points on its own bench too, most notably Drake Maye's 32.4, which would have beaten Prescott's 22.7 by nearly 10. Terry McLaurin's 8.8 would also have topped Waddle's 0.7. Those misses did not matter in the end, since a team with no active manager still won by 4.

With the loss, Dawgs finished sixth of six and Mekhi became the league's last-place finisher for 2025, the first manager other than Sonny to hold the title. It ended Sonny's run in the Bum Bowl standings in the same season he went from last place to champion, so the bottom spot passed from the commissioner straight to Kai. For a manager widely regarded as one of the most knowledgeable in the league, and a team that scored the kind of points Dawgs did, the finish was an outlier.

Ramon's Remains finished fifth of six, and the win went on Ramon's record with the league's customary asterisk. The result became one of the defining entries in the story of a team that kept winning after its manager was removed, and Brucie was credited with avoiding last place in a game he had no part in. He returned in 2026 to run No Banner only HULK, while Mekhi returned to run Dawgs in the expanded eight-team league.

The 2025 Bum Bowl is remembered mainly for its tight end slot. A zero-point starter with 10.7 points on the bench, in a game lost by 4, settled who would carry the league's last-place mark into the 2026 season.
